title: Audit storage lifecycle SLOs and pipeline failure playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the intended storage lifecycle (hot/warm/cold/archive) for Redwood audit logs, the SLOs we expect for retention and queryability, and concrete pipeline implementation notes for indexing and backfills. It focuses on operational failure modes and pragmatic runbook steps to restore searchable evidence for compliance/forensics and SIEM export consumers.

High-level goals / constraints:
- All audit events must be retained raw for 2 years (regulatory requirement placeholder) with metadata indexed for 180 days for fast queries.
- Search/query SLOs: 95th percentile query latency for indexed data (last 30d) < 350ms; 99th < 2s for common API/actor/time queries.
- Durability SLO: <= 1 in 10,000 events lost during normal operation.
- SIEM export (near-real-time) should deliver >= 99% of events to external SIEM within 10 minutes of ingestion for the last 30 days.
- Cost objective: cold/archive tiers should be used for >95% of storage after 90 days to limit egress and hot-node footprint.

Retention tiers (recommended):
- Hot index: 0-30 days. Full inverted-index + doc values for fast search, stored in OpenSearch hot nodes (SSD).
- Warm index: 31-90 days. Read-optimized, fewer replicas; allow slower queries.
- Cold index: 91-365 days. Compressed storage (frozen indices or object-store backed indices). Query capability retained but higher latency.
- Archive blobs: 365d - 2 years. Raw event blobs stored in object storage (S3-compatible), indexed metadata reduced to minimal pointers and checksums. Retrieval requires rehydration/backfill.

Schema/indexing notes:
- Audit event canonical fields (index time): event_id, timestamp, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_id, resource_type, outcome(success|fail), request_id, trace_id, ingestion_shard, original_blob_path, schema_version.
- Use append-only partitioning by day (YYYY.MM.DD) for indices to simplify retention and rollups.
- Include a lightweight ingestion metadata document per blob that records blob_checksum, blob_size, kinesis_offset (or kafka_partition/offset), kms_key_id, and ingest_timestamp.
- Index mapping must include keyword sub-fields for actor_id/resource_id for fast filtering and a flattened field for unstructured meta (avoid deeply nested).

Indexing pipeline (core flow):
1) Event gen -> blob writer (parquet/ndjson) -> object store staged path (s3://audit-raw/yyyy/mm/dd/blob-UUID).
2) Event metadata message sent to message bus (Kafka) with blob pointer + offsets.
3) Indexer consumer reads metadata message, downloads blob (streaming), parses events, transforms to indexable docs, bulk-indexs into current day index.
4) Acks written back to offset-tracker and blob manifest updated with index status per blob.
5) SIEM export connector tails the index and/or listens to Kafka topic for near-RT delivery.

Backfill strategy (principles):
- Idempotent ingestion: indexer must be idempotent keyed by event_id and blob_checksum to avoid duplicates.
- Checkpointed workers: backfills run with clearly versioned checkpoints (date range + shard + job-id) to resume mid-way without overlap.
- Throttled concurrency to avoid resource saturation: adaptive rate limits based on cluster health metrics (CPU, GC, indexing vs query rate).
- Prioritize metadata reindexing first for quick queryability; full document reindex as lower priority.
- Use a staging reindex index and switch alias when ready to minimize search disruption.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
1) Consumer lag (Kafka backlog grows)
   - Symptom: backlog spikes, SIEM latency increases, last_written_timestamp falls behind.
   - Immediate action: increase consumer parallelism if cluster capacity allows; spawn temporary indexer pods with limited concurrency.
   - If due to downstream OpenSearch slowness, throttle consumers and increase retention in message bus; alert SRE.

2) Partial indexing / malformed records in blob
   - Symptom: bulk-index error rates spike, manifest shows partial success.
   - Immediate action: isolate offending blob by copying to quarantine prefix; run blob-local parser (dev-container) to reproduce error.
   - Fix: patch parser to tolerate minor schema drift or schedule a targeted backfill of cleaned blobs.

3) Duplicate events (reprocessing without idempotence)
   - Symptom: duplicate event_id counts; mismatch between blob manifest and index.
   - Mitigation: run dedupe job that de-duplicates index by event_id; mark impacted index segments as repaired.

4) Corrupt blobs or missing object-store objects
   - Symptom: indexer fails to download blob or checksum mismatch.
   - Action: consult backup tier/replication (S3 versioning), request re-upload from producer if available, or mark as unrecoverable and surface to compliance with event counts and gaps.

5) KMS/HSM failures when decrypting blobs
   - Symptom: indexer throws decryption errors for many blobs.
   - Action: alert security/KMS team immediately. Use emergency workflow to switch to fallback keys if policy allows.

6) SIEM sink failure (throttling or auth failures)
   - Symptom: queued delivery backlog, 5xx responses from SIEM, increased retry.
   - Action: temporarily buffer to durable queue, notify SIEM ops, apply exponential backoff. If persistent, enable a lower-fidelity export (headers+metadata only) to maintain compliance.

Operational runbook (triage template):
- Pager receives alert -> document incident ID and initial impact (time window, % events delayed/lost).
- Check consumer lag metrics for indexing and SIEM export.
- Inspect indexer pod logs for repeated exceptions (parser, decryption, bulk rejection).
- Check storage layer: object-store health, recent 5xxs, KMS errors.
- If cluster health OK and backlog present -> scale indexer workers conservatively.
- If bulk errors due to mapping incompatibility -> create a temporary mapping patch: (a) index into a new mapping with additional fields as text/keyword; (b) re-run backfill.
- Communication: use template:
  - "Incident ID: {id} - audit-indexing impact from {start} to {end}. We're currently reprocessing {n} blobs. Expected time to restore searchable state: {eta}."

Backfill implementation notes (practical):
- Backfill jobs should be executed from a central controller that:
  - calculates affected blobs by date range and manifests,
  - verifies checksums before processing,
  - writes progress to a shared checkpoint table (DynamoDB/Postgres),
  - emits per-job metrics (processed_count, success_rate, error_types, throughput).
- Support two modes: fast-path metadata-only (index minimal metadata to restore queryability) and full-content reindex (rebuild complete document fields).
- Provide a dry-run mode that validates mapping compatibility and estimates index size.

Monitoring + alerting (recommended metrics & thresholds):
- Indexer consumer lag (events/min backlog) -> warn > 10k/min, critical > 100k/min for > 15m.
- Indexing error rate -> warn > 0.5% over 5m, critical > 2% over 5m.
- Bulk rejection rate (OpenSearch 4xx/429) -> warn > 1% 5m.
- SIEM sink error rate -> warn > 1% 5m, critical > 5% 10m.
- Blob download failure rate -> warn > 0.1% 5m.
- Compression/decompression failures -> critical immediate.

Testing strategy for resilience:
- Chaos tests: randomly delete and restore ephemeral index nodes; verify backfill can recover within expected window.
- Replay tests: run periodic replays of 1 week of traffic into a staging index to validate that ingestion code handles schema evolution.
- Cost tests: simulated reindex of 30-90d volumes to estimate cpu/io impact and cost.

SLA and business expectations:
- Normal operation: searchable for events in hot/warm indices within 5 minutes of ingestion (indexing SLO).
- Degraded: if backfill required, metadata-only recovery for a given day within 48 hours; full-content reindex within 7 days for business-critical time ranges.
- Notify compliance owners if any day has >0 unrecoverable events after 30 days of remediation attempts.

Open questions / TODO:
- Confirm exact regulatory retention windows (compliance to confirm 2 years vs 7 years for specific customers).
- Decide whether to rely on OpenSearch frozen indices vs custom object-store backed indexing for cold tier (cost tradeoffs).
- Policy for sensitive data: should some audit events be archived sooner or redacted before indexing? (privacy/reg/legal input needed).
- Finalize SIEM contract SLAs to define acceptable export latency and loss tolerances.

Appendix: quick command examples / helpers:
- Re-run backfill for date range (pseudo): python ops/backfill.py --start 2024-01-01 --end 2024-01-07 --mode metadata-only --parallel 8 --job-id bf-202401
- Check index health: curl -s -u user:pass https://opensearch.internal/_cluster/health?pretty
- Identify stale manifests: SELECT blob_path FROM audit_manifests WHERE indexed_at IS NULL AND created_at < '2024-02-01';

Contacts: Rafael Ortiz (indexing lead), Priya Nair (compliance), Samir Patel (SRE oncall).

Notes to self: prioritize building a small "reindex-linter" that scans a sample of blobs to detect schema drift and produce a small mapping patch automatically.

End of doc.
